sentences.text:
This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Appeal by injured-claimant aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 27.12.2016 passed in MVC No.715/2014 on the file of the Member, MACT-XIII and IV Additional District Judge, Vijayapura ('Tribunal').
2. Brief facts of the case are that:
a) On 05.07.2013 at about 11.10 p.m., on Old Kumbar Naka Road near Buvaji Medical Stores, driver of NC: 2023:KHC-K:8640 City Bus bearing No.MH-04/G-1593 drove the bus in rash and negligent manner from backside and dashed against the appellant, in which appellant sustained injuries.
The appellant was shifted to Government Hospital, Solapur and he was under treatment for one month as an inpatient.
He underwent operation for more than two occasions and due to fracture, right leg was amputed above knee.
Even after discharge from hospital he underwent several treatments.

Due to disability he is unable to carry his regular work, therefore he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-, contending that he was working as a Tailor and due to accidental injuries he became completely disabled.

2 b)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On service of notice respondent No.1 - owner of the offending bus remained absent, respondent No.2- Insurance Company filed statement of objections denying the petition averments, manner of accident, injuries and avocation of the claimant.
Tribunal framed issues and NC: 2023:KHC-K:8640 recorded evidence.
Claimant examined himself as PW1, examined the treated Dr. S.P. Handarlmath as PW2 and exhibited 11 documents at Exs.P1 to P11.
On behalf of respondents except marking copy of the policy no witness has been examined.

c) The Tribunal on appreciation of the evidence held that the accident had occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, however, attributed 20% negligence on the part of claimant.
Taking income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/- per month and assessing disability at 75%, the Tribunal awarded Rs.10,93,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
Seeking enhancement of said compensation, claimant is before this Court.

3. Sri S.S. Mamadapur, learned counsel for the appellant reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of appeal submits that the Tribunal grossly NC: 2023:KHC-K:8640 erred in attributing negligence at 20% on the part of claimant merely because in the cross-examination, he had stated that he had not seen the vehicle while crossing the road, which is taken out of context.

He further submits that the claimant has examined the treated Doctor who in his deposition has stated that the claimant has suffered 85% of disability and there was no reason for the Tribunal to reduce the disability to 75%.
Considering the nature of avocation the claimant ought to have been considered as 100% disabled.
He submits that the compensation awarded under other heads also is on the lower side, hence, seeks for enhancement.

4. Learned counsel Sri Sudarshan M., for respondent - Insurance Company justifying the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal submits that assessment of disability at 75% cannot be stated to be low.

He submits that the Tribunal taking into consideration all the material evidence placed on record, more particularly, the admission made by the claimant NC: 2023:KHC-K:8640 himself, has attributed 20% negligence on the part of claimant in causing the accident, the same warrants no interference.
The grant of compensation under other heads is also justified.
Hence, he seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
6.
The accident in question resulting in injuries consequently leading to amputation of right leg above knee level of the claimant is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant was a pedestrian and the offending bus had hit him from behind.
The width of the road is stated to be 50 feet.
The accident is stated to have occurred when claimant was trying to cross the road to go to medical shop on the other side of the road.
In other words the accident stated to have occurred in a busy market place.
It is settled law that negligence can be attributed on the one who is expected to avoid the NC: 2023:KHC-K:8640 accident at the last minute.

In the instant case, since accident has admittedly taken place at crowded area, it was expected that the driver of the offending vehicle to be more cautious, more particularly, towards the pedestrians.
The severity of the accident would reveal that the driver of the offending vehicle ought to have been extra cautious considering the place where the accident has taken place.

The Tribunal at Para 11 of the impugned judgment has noted a Sri. Srinivas vs The Manager And Anr on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156182584/
3 part of the deposition of claimant wherein he has stated that "he was proceeding from the left side of the road to right side of the road and that he had crossed the road without looking at the other vehicles on the road".

entities.text: Sri. Srinivas vs The Manager And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said statement has been taken by the Tribunal as evidence enough to attribute 20% of negligence on the part of claimant.
Thus, in the considered view of this Court, it cannot be the basis in the absence of any cogent evidence to hold that the claimant was negligent.
No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents to prove the negligence on the part of the claimant.
The stray admission in the deposition cannot be the basis to NC: 2023:KHC-K:8640 attribute negligence in the absence of any cogent evidence.
The finding of the Tribunal attributing 20% negligence on the part of claimant therefore requires to be interfered with.
Hence, it is set aside.
7. As regards assessment of disability is concerned, the claimant has examined none other than the treated Doctor, who has opined that the claimant has suffered 85% of the disability.
Nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination to disbelieve the said deposition of PW2.
However, the Tribunal has taken the same at 75%, while the counsel for the appellant insists that the disability considering the nature of avocation of the claimant has to be assessed at 100%.
The injury has resulted amputation of right leg above knee level.
The claimant stated to have been carrying on the avocation of Tailor.
In that view of the matter, no doubt, claimant requires the dominant usage of the right leg, but it cannot be said that he has rendered 100% disability.

This Court NC:
2023:KHC-K:8640 is of the view that the disability of 80% would be justified.
Therefore, disability is assessed at 80%.
8. The assessment of notional income of Rs.7,000/- per month is maintained.

Further, in the light of the law laid down in the case of Erudhaya Priya Versus State Express Transport Corporation Ltd. -
2020 SCC OnLine SC 601 claimant suffering injuries of this nature would also entitled for future prospects.

2020 SCC OnLine SC 601
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the age of the claimant being 36 years, 40% of his income has to be added towards future prospects.

9. Calculated as above, loss of future income would be:
Rs.7000 + 40% of 7000 i.e., 2,800/- = 9800/- Rs.9,800/- x 12 x 15 x 80% =
Rs.14,11,200/-
10.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.67,000/- towards special diet, conveyance and attendant charges; a sum of Rs.1,75,000/- towards future medical expenses; a - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8640 sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities of life and a sum of Rs.29,130/- towards medical expenses
, the same are maintained as it is.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering, the same is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/- by adding Rs.50,000/-.
In all the claimant is entitled for Rs.18,82,330/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization as against the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

12. The appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
